title: AppLovin Jumps 16% After Hours on 55% Revenue Growth; Qualcomm Slips on Soft Sales
dek: AppLovin and Qualcomm both reported after the close on Wednesday. AppLovin's revenue rose 55% and its shares climbed in extended trading; Qualcomm's revenue fell 8% and its shares slipped.
author: Meridian Newsroom

body:
## Two companies, two very different reactions

Two companies reported results after the close on Wednesday, Nov. 4. AppLovin and Qualcomm are the names confirmed in CNBC's live coverage as reporting after the bell (CNBC, via Stock Titan). The reactions split sharply.

## AppLovin: revenue and profit both up

AppLovin said third-quarter revenue rose 55% to a record $2.18 billion for the quarter ended Sept. 30. Net income grew 72% to $1.44 billion, and the company cited an industry-leading net-income margin of 66% (MarketScreener, summarizing the company release). The company also said it repurchased and withheld 4.1 million Class A shares during the quarter (AppLovin release, via Stock Titan).

In extended trading, the stock rose 16.29% at 4:16 p.m. ET, against a $271.75 close (CNBC, via Stock Titan). That move is an after-hours price, not a regular-session close, and it may change at the next open.

## Qualcomm: a revenue decline and a modest guide

Qualcomm reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $10.32 billion for the quarter ended Sept. 27, down 8% from a year earlier. It expects revenue of $10.4 billion to $11.2 billion in the current quarter (Qualcomm release, via Stock Titan). The company's release is available on its investor relations site, and this story relies on the figures as reported by CNBC and Stock Titan.

Shares fell 4.44% in extended trading, against a $173.19 close (CNBC, via Stock Titan). The drop came on a day when the broader market rallied on the midterm result and lower oil prices.

## What to watch

The reactions suggest investors are paying for growth. AppLovin's double-digit revenue growth and margin lifted the stock, while Qualcomm's revenue decline weighed on it. The next checkpoint is the regular-session trade on Thursday, when after-hours moves are tested against the open.

*AI-assisted analysis. Not financial advice.*
